subject: social
name: Social Studies
title: Grade 7 Social Studies: Medieval & Early Modern World History
overview: Grade 7 Social Studies engages students in historical inquiry, primary source analysis, geographic mapping, and civic deliberation aligned with the C3 Framework.
competencies: Corroborate primary documents with historical context and point-of-view analysis.
Explain how geographical trade networks and physical barriers shaped civilizations.
Analyze economic developments, resource allocation, and market exchanges.
Assess the evolution of democratic values, civil liberties, and civic responsibilities.

modules.title: The Islamic World, Trans-Saharan Kingdoms & Eurasian Trade
modules.description: Examining the expansion of the Islamic Caliphates, the Golden Age of scholarship, West African kingdoms, and trade networks.

topics.title: The Islamic Golden Age and Cultural Diffusion
topics.description: Tracing scientific, mathematical, and medical innovations from Baghdad and Cordoba across Afro-Eurasia.

topics.title: Kingdoms of West Africa: Ghana, Mali and Songhai
topics.description: Investigating trans-Saharan gold and salt trade, Mansa Musa's pilgrimage, and university scholarship in Timbuktu.

modules.title: Medieval Europe, the Mongol Empire & the Black Death
modules.description: Analyzing feudalism, the Catholic Church, the Crusades, the Pax Mongolica, and the devastating impact of the bubonic plague.

topics.title: Feudalism, Manorialism and the Crusades
topics.description: Examining medieval European social hierarchies, knights, serfdom, and religious wars in the Holy Land.

topics.title: The Mongol Empire and the Black Death Pandemic
topics.description: Evaluating Genghis Khan's military strategies, trade along the Silk Road, and the social collapse caused by the Plague.

modules.title: The Renaissance, Scientific Inquiry & the Reformation
modules.description: Investigating the rebirth of arts and humanism in Italy, the invention of the printing press, and religious reformations.

topics.title: Italian and Northern Renaissance Humanism
topics.description: Analyzing perspective in art (da Vinci, Michelangelo) and the literary rise of secular humanism.

topics.title: The Printing Press and the Protestant Reformation
topics.description: Evaluating Gutenberg's movable type, Martin Luther's Ninety-Five Theses, and religious fragmentation in Europe.
